summary: Two-project integration brief: Agent Loop proposes autonomous work (README.md:53), while Tool Gate deterministically evaluates caller-supplied tool metadata and invocation envelopes and emits allow, deny, or review_required receipts without executing tools (README.md:5-13,17-20). Their shared safety boundary is the handoff between proposed action and runtime execution: Agent Loop should never invoke the runtime directly, and Tool Gate decisions must be enforced before side effects. Actionable integration: adapt every Agent Loop tool proposal into ToolMetadata plus InvocationEnvelope, call Tool Gate, execute only allow receipts, route review_required to an operator, and audit every receipt. Agent Loop risk: any direct execution path would bypass policy review. Tool Gate risk: it trusts caller-supplied metadata and is not a sandbox or authorization layer, so inaccurate mutates_state, risk, or target declarations can produce unsafe decisions (README.md:10-13,156-158). The declared clean-tree check passed, and no files were modified.
